record.paper_title: A survey of equivariant map algebras with open problems
record.original_question: Let X be an affine scheme with coordinate algebra A, let a be a finite-dimensional algebra, and let an algebraic group Γ act completely reducibly on both A and a by automorphisms. For the resulting equivariant map algebra M(X,a)^Γ, classify the irreducible finite-dimensional representations when Γ is allowed to be more general than a finite group.

evidence.quote: (a) More general groups Γ. Instead of a finite group Γ, one can consider, for instance, an algebraic group acting completely reducibly on A and a. The first step in the study of the resulting EMAs would be to classify their irreducible finite- dimensional representations.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $X$ be an affine scheme over an algebraically closed field of characteristic zero, with coordinate algebra $A = \mathcal{O}(X)$, and let $\mathfrak{a}$ be a finite-dimensional Lie algebra. Let $\Gamma$ be an algebraic group acting on $A$ by algebra automorphisms and on $\mathfrak{a}$ by Lie algebra automorphisms, in such a way that both $A$ and $\mathfrak{a}$ are completely reducible as $\Gamma$-modules. Form the equivariant map algebra
$$M(X,\mathfrak{a})^{\Gamma} := (A \otimes \mathfrak{a})^{\Gamma},$$
the Lie subalgebra of $\Gamma$-invariants in $A \otimes \mathfrak{a}$ (equivalently, the Lie algebra of $\Gamma$-equivariant regular maps $X \to \mathfrak{a}$).

Classify, up to isomorphism, the irreducible finite-dimensional representations of $M(X,\mathfrak{a})^{\Gamma}$ in this generality, where $\Gamma$ is allowed to be an arbitrary (not necessarily finite) algebraic group acting completely reducibly as above. In particular, determine whether every such irreducible finite-dimensional representation is isomorphic to a tensor product of evaluation representations and a one-dimensional representation, and identify the precise parameter set classifying these representations.
artifact.status_search_result: The classification of irreducible finite-dimensional representations of equivariant map algebras is well-established when $\Gamma$ is a finite group (Neher–Savage–Senesi, 2009/2012), where the irreducibles are tensor products of evaluation representations with a one-dimensional representation. The generalization to arbitrary algebraic groups acting completely reducibly is explicitly listed as an open direction; web searches did not surface a published full classification in this broader generality, although related work has appeared (e.g. on equivariant map superalgebras, extensions and block decompositions). Status appears to remain open or only partially addressed in special cases.

status_evidence.title: Irreducible finite-dimensional representations of equivariant map algebras
status_evidence.snippet: Classification of irreducible finite-dimensional representations of equivariant map algebras as tensor products of evaluation representations and one-dimensional representations (finite group setting).
status_evidence.claim: The finite-group case is solved, motivating the more general algebraic-group question.

status_evidence.title: Extensions and block decompositions for finite-dimensional representations of equivariant map algebras
status_evidence.snippet: Describes extensions between irreducible finite-dimensional representations for X an affine scheme of finite type and g reductive, in the finite-group equivariant setting.
status_evidence.claim: Subsequent work focuses on the finite-group setting; no full classification for arbitrary algebraic groups Γ is reported.

status_evidence.title: A survey of equivariant map algebras with open problems
status_evidence.snippet: Lists generalization to algebraic groups Γ acting completely reducibly as an open direction; first step is to classify irreducible finite-dimensional representations.
status_evidence.claim: The problem is explicitly posed as open in the survey context.
